transcript:
Header: 2027-06-29 10:30 PDT | Duration: ~42m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Orion Head of ML), Carlos Mendes (Orion Infra), Leah Ortiz (Orion Product)

--- Summary / Topics ---
- Model selection: redwood catalog variants, quantized vs fp16, latency/cost tradeoffs
- Pinning & rollbacks: version pinning, fallback to smaller model family on capacity loss
- Security & deployment: VPC, KMS, SOC2 notes and perf benchmarking on dedicated nodes

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick agenda review, we'll go over the evals you ran last week, then model pinning options and plan a benchmark on dedicated capacity
00:18 Priya Singh: yup thanks, we want to focus on latency at peak and any quality delta, the product team needs p95 under 420ms for short chat flows
00:30 Ethan Park: got it, we also have the last run from the catalog, we compared redwood-2.7b-q4 and redwood-7b-fp16 and there were some hallucination differences on the financial QAs
00:45 Leah Ortiz: can you explain the q4 vs fp16 stuff a bit in plain english?
00:52 Ethan Park: sure, q4 is quantized 4-bit which lowers memory and cost but sometimes degrades rare-token generation and factuality in our tests, fp16 preserves more precision but costs more and uses more GPU RAM
01:10 Carlos Mendes: our infra constraint is that we only have limited VPC capacity for pilot, so if fp16 needs bigger instances we need to know instance types and whether Redwood Dedicated can autoscale for bursts
01:25 Maya Chen: yes Dedicated supports autoscaling and burst lanes, we'll include the instance sizing sheet. For the pilot we can pin a model variant and still allow automatic fallback to a smaller variant if capacity constrained
01:40 Priya Singh: about the quality delta — we saw on the insurance Q/A test set redwood-2.7b-q4 had 3.4% lower accuracy vs 7b fp16 on named-entity recall, that's a concern for compliance; do you have recommended rollbacks?
01:58 Ethan Park: recommended pattern: pin to the 7b-fp16 for production-critical routes, but create a fallback route to 2.7b-q4 for cost-sensitive or non-critical tasks. Also you can do prefix caching to speed up common prompts which helps latency without changing model.
02:20 Leah Ortiz: and pinning means if we push a new model version we don't automatically get moved?
02:26 Maya Chen: correct, pinning locks the route to a model version; rollouts can be done via canary or A/B and you can configure automatic rollback if quality metrics dip beyond threshold
02:42 Priya Singh: what about rollback latency — like if a new model introduces regressions, how fast can you switch?
02:50 Ethan Park: switching is near-instant for routing (seconds) but warmup for KV cache and latency profile takes a couple minutes; we're working on warm-start helpers. For safety you can set a traffic failover to a pinned older model to avoid warmup impact
03:10 Carlos Mendes: security question — we need to ensure keys never leave our KMS and audit logs are retained for 365 days. Is that supported in the private deployment?
03:20 Maya Chen: yes Private supports customer-managed KMS and extended audit retention as an add-on. For Dedicated we can enable KMS integration and send audit logs to your S3 with lifecycle policies
03:36 Priya Singh: we also want SAML SSO and RBAC for the console, plus per-route access controls
03:44 Ethan Park: SAML SSO is supported and we can map to RBAC roles; per-route access is in the console now, we can demo in the security deep dive
03:58 Maya Chen: ok back to the benchmarks — Ethan can you summarize the last runs?
04:04 Ethan Park: sure, short summary: hosted redwood-7b-fp16 p50 ~ 180ms for 128-token responses, p95 ~ 420ms in eu-west region under synthetic load; q4 variant p50 ~ 130ms p95 ~ 360ms but the quality delta on named entity recall and hallucination was visible on the 1k eval set. On Dedicated nodes with batching we expect similar p50 but better cost per token and more predictable p95 under sustained load
04:36 Priya Singh: what's the model catalog versioning like — how do we know which build is 7b-fp16 v1.2 vs v1.3?
04:44 Ethan Park: each model artifact has a version tag, and the console shows the commit hash and performance profile. Pinning takes the tag/hash so you remain on that variant until you change it
05:00 Leah Ortiz: any gotchas around quantization that could surprise us later?
05:06 Ethan Park: yeah quantization can change distribution of logits slightly; for low-frequency facts it can diverge. We recommend running your invariance tests and having canary traffic on new quantized models before wide rollout
05:24 Priya Singh: for our success criteria — we need p95 < 420ms for chat, and quality delta <1.5% on entity recall vs baseline. If those are met we move to a 3-month reserved Dedicated pilot
05:38 Maya Chen: that aligns with our proposal, we'll run the dedicated benchmark and share it. Also will include fallback policy examples for auto rollback and how to configure thresholds
05:52 Carlos Mendes: for the dedicated benchmark do you need our sample dataset or can you run with synthetic?
05:58 Ethan Park: ideally both — synthetic for load characteristics and your sample prompts for quality; please upload a sanitized subset to the shared drive, or we can run on-prem if you prefer Private pilot
06:15 Priya Singh: we'll upload a cleaned set of 3 prompt templates and 2 eval metrics by next week as discussed
06:25 Maya Chen: great. last thing — pricing and contract: we'll send an updated pilot pricing with reserved tier and burst capacity options and a short pilot SOW
06:38 Leah Ortiz: thanks, sounds good to me
06:41 Maya Chen: recap of next steps: Ethan runs dedicated benchmarks, Maya sends pricing and SOW, Priya uploads prompts, Carlos confirms VPC peering requirements and security contact, schedule security deep dive for next week. Any final questions?
06:55 Priya Singh: none from me, thanks
07:00 Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with artifacts
